## Purpose and Repository Shape
This is a Java DSA/interview-preparation course repository, not a unified application or library. It combines ordered curriculum material, standalone Java demonstrations, and assignments. The progression is defined by `SYLLABUS.md`, `assignments/`, and sequential `lectures/` directories.

## Entry Points and Execution Model
Each lecture code folder is independently runnable; many contain a `Main.java` or topic-specific executable such as `StackMain.java` and `QueueMain.java`. There is no root build, package, deployment entry point, or shared runtime. Java code is generally organized under `com.kunal` for IntelliJ-style projects, while later examples are often flat Java source folders.
- `lectures/05-first-java-program/first-idea-program/src/com/kunal/Main.java`
- `lectures/19-stacks-n-queues/code/src/com/kunal/StackMain.java`
- `lectures/20-trees/code/introduction/Main.java`

## Curriculum and Assignment Boundary
Lecture directories are the canonical instructional sequence: concepts, PDFs/notes, then illustrative implementations. Assignments are separate Markdown problem sets mapped to early/mid-course topics; solutions are intentionally not integrated into the repository.
- `assignments/01-flow-of-program.md`
- `assignments/14-oop.md`
- `assignments/18-heaps.md`

## Foundational Java and Algorithm Stages
The first stages establish Java syntax, console input/output, branching, methods, arrays, then searching and elementary sorting. Examples are small self-contained programs that accept values or initialize in-memory inputs, run an algorithm, and print results.
- `lectures/05-first-java-program/first-idea-program/src/com/kunal/Inputs.java`
- `lectures/09-linear search/code/src/com/kunal/SearchIn2DArray.java`
- `lectures/10-binary search/code/src/com/kunal/BinarySearch.java`

## Recursive, Mathematical, and Complexity Techniques
Recursion is the first substantial internal organization: packages separate introductory recursion, arrays, strings, backtracking, and recursive sorting. Later math/bitwise and complexity lessons provide supporting algorithmic techniques rather than reusable shared utilities.
- `lectures/14-recursion/code/src/com/kunal/backtracking/SudokuSolver.java`
- `lectures/14-recursion/code/src/com/kunal/sorting/MergeSort.java`
- `lectures/16-math/code/src/com/kunal/maths/Seive.java`

## Object Modeling and Core Data Structures
OOP lessons model language mechanisms—inheritance, polymorphism, interfaces, generics, exceptions—through deliberately local example class graphs. Data-structure lessons implement mutable structures and expose operations through their local drivers; this is the principal code dependency boundary within each topic.
- `lectures/17-oop/code/src/com/kunal/properties/inheritance/Box.java`
- `lectures/18-linkedlist/code/src/com/kunal/LL.java`
- `lectures/19-stacks-n-queues/code/src/com/kunal/CustomStack.java`

## Advanced Structures and Algorithms
The later curriculum expands into trees, heaps, hash maps, advanced sorting, compression, and square-root decomposition. Implementations remain independently scoped per lesson; for example, trees include BST, AVL, segment-tree, traversal, and interview-question variants rather than one common tree package.
- `lectures/20-trees/code/AVL/AVL.java`
- `lectures/20-trees/code/Segment trees/SegmentTree.java`
- `lectures/27-huffman-coding/code/HuffmanCoder.java`

## Runtime, Infrastructure, and External Services
Material runtime is the Java/JDK standard library, exercised as console programs; IDE metadata indicates IntelliJ modules and some Eclipse/Replit project artifacts. There are no declared third-party dependencies, databases, APIs, CI/CD, cloud infrastructure, or persistent service integrations. The README links externally to YouTube/course content, while repository-local PDFs and notes are the primary learning assets.
- `README.md`
- `lectures/20-trees/code/AVL/.project`
- `lectures/23-file handling/code/Output.java`
